findings.opaque_snapshot: A commit/tree SHA is a content-addressed snapshot identity. Without inspecting tree entries or possessing a precommitted expected root, it does not prove required-member completeness, current generation, semantic correctness, or an aggregate value. Treating the opaque hash itself as terminal produces false terminality in 376/384 finite scenarios.
findings.precommitted_exact_root: If every expected byte/path is known before execution, exact tree-hash equality can certify that exact snapshot without reading other-role semantics. In this lattice it terminalizes only 2/384 scenarios and false-excludes 382/384; all 192 dynamic-output scenarios are unsupported because their expected bytes are not known before execution. Concurrent unrelated/disjoint tree changes also make exact whole-tree equality brittle.
findings.tree_scan: Git tree inspection can answer path/blob-SHA questions, but it requires other-role metadata. Current frozen CLEAN policy forbids other-worker state/output reads, so this is not a current role-authorized route.
findings.merkle_proof_surface: A hypothetical sanitized inclusion/completeness proof surface would avoid raw other-role path enumeration, but current GitHub Trees documentation does not expose such a custom role-aware proof API and current control does not authorize one. Even a correct inclusion proof for a dynamic unknown blob hash does not prove the payload's semantics; all 192 dynamic-output proof scenarios remain semantically uncertified.
findings.semantic_reducer: A reducer can compute more useful cross-role predicates and aggregate values, but all 384 reducer scenarios require other-role metadata and content reads and are therefore outside current CLEAN policy.
findings.response_loss: An opaque current snapshot SHA does not resolve whether an earlier proposed publication occurred if the branch subsequently moved because of a concurrent disjoint write; all 96 response-loss plus concurrent-write scenarios remain unreconciled without persistent transition identity/ancestry evidence.

public_source_observations.observation: Git is content-addressable; tree objects record filenames and blob/subtree object IDs, and commits point to a tree snapshot. This supports snapshot commitment/identity, not semantic correctness of unknown payloads.

GitHub Trees API exposes tree entry path/mode/type/SHA metadata and create/get-tree operations. Using that metadata for other roles would be a cross-role semantic/metadata read under the current CLEAN boundary; the current docs do not expose a custom sanitized role-completeness Merkle-proof primitive.

clean_boundary_assessment.opaque_commit_or_tree_sha_read: compatible only as transport/snapshot identity when no other-role semantics are inferred
clean_boundary_assessment.custom_sanitized_merkle_proof_service: unavailable capability and unresolved child, not acceptance
clean_boundary_assessment.semantic_reducer: forbidden because it must inspect other-role metadata/content
clean_boundary_assessment.largest_current_clean_value: self-local snapshot/provenance identity and independently terminal role-local effects; no generic cross-role completeness or semantic aggregate proof

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_transport: Git object/ref APIs only; no Actions/Codespaces/artifact/LFS/package/cloud compute
zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.custom_proof_or_reducer: not accepted; would be new unavailable/external capability

exact_continuation: Next leaf: self-local proof-carrying result contracts. Test whether each role can emit an independently verifiable root-bound certificate whose useful outcome is terminal without any cross-role reader. Compare schema-plus-content-hash contract, deterministic local predicate proof, root/control tuple binding, self-contained proof-carrying artifact, and plain hash negative control. Include valid hash with wrong semantics, stale control tuple, omitted required evidence field, duplicate replay, role add, response loss, and a requirement for all-role completeness. Treat any verifier that must enumerate other-role certificates or any external proof service as an unresolved child. Target the largest self-certifying outcome class that remains fully executable under current CLEAN isolation.
